idea-plugin.name: Peek Definition
idea-plugin.description:
Peek Definition for Java. It shows the definition of the symbol at the caret right below the current line, inside the editor you are working in, so you can read an implementation without leaving your file or losing your place.

Unlike Quick Definition, the Peek is not a popup: it does not cover your code, it stays open while you keep working, and you can open several at once.

Features

  • Embedded in the editor: the definition opens between the lines of your code, with the lines below moved down instead of hidden.
  • Just the definition: the Peek shows only the method, with its signature and module in the header, like Quick Definition. Switch to the whole file or turn on line numbers from the ⋮ menu; your choice is remembered for the next Peek. It is a real editor on the real file: it uses your color scheme, font and theme, Ctrl+Click works inside it, and it updates live when the file changes.
  • Accurate: definitions are resolved the same way as Go to Declaration, so overloads, constructors and library classes (attached or decompiled sources) resolve correctly.
  • Implementations: peeking an interface or abstract method adds a dropdown to the header listing its implementations, like Quick Definition; pick one to show it in the same Peek.
  • Several Peeks at once: peek from different lines and every Peek stays open. Peeking from inside a Peek replaces its content with the new definition.
  • Read-only: opening, switching and closing a Peek never modifies your code.

Usage

  • Put the caret on a method call or constructor and choose Peek Definition from the editor's right-click menu or from Navigate.
  • Click the Peek's title bar to collapse or expand it. Its Open in Editor button opens the file in a regular editor tab.
  • The ⋮ menu in the header opens the file in an editor tab, switches between the method only and the whole file, and shows or hides line numbers.
  • Esc inside a Peek (or its × button) closes that Peek. Esc in the editor closes all of its Peeks.

No shortcut is assigned by default. Bind one in Settings | Keymap | Peek Definition.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.1.1

  • Implementations: peeking an interface or abstract method adds a dropdown to the header listing its implementations; pick one to show it in the same Peek.
  • Shows only the method by default. Switch to the whole file, or turn on line numbers, from the new ⋮ menu; the choice is remembered for the next Peek.
  • Header redesigned after Quick Definition: the definition's icon and signature, plus its module or library.
  • New Open in Editor button in the header. Double-clicking the title no longer opens the file, so it can't be triggered by accident; clicking the title still collapses or expands the Peek.
  • The Peek stands out more from the surrounding code: rounded outline in the theme's accent color, header in the tool window color, and a slightly tinted background.

0.0.1

  • Initial release: Peek Definition for Java, embedded below the current line.
